headline: 14 arrested over land dispute attacks in Mohammadpur and Adabor
summary: Police held suspects in two separate incidents involving land-grabbing attempts and a building attack with sharp weapons in Dhaka.
details: Police arrested 14 people following two separate attacks linked to land disputes in Dhaka's Mohammadpur and Adabor areas. Eight suspects were held for an attempted land grab in Mohammadpur's Chand Udyan, while six others were arrested for attacking a building in Adabor.

In the Mohammadpur incident, a group of 150 to 200 people allegedly broke into an office, tore down a tin fence, and vandalized the property on Saturday. CCTV footage showed the group breaking locks and removing items from the site.

Two of the arrested individuals, Md Limon and Md Monowar Hossain Saddam, reportedly admitted to taking part in land-grabbing activities for money. Both had previous criminal records involving mugging and fighting.

In the Adabor attack, a group of 20 to 25 people used sharp weapons to attack a house on Road 6 of the Shyamoli Housing project. They damaged the gate, windows, and CCTV cameras during the assault on Saturday morning.
Relatives of the building owner alleged that the property had been previously seized by a local man after August 5, 2024, but was regained through legal proceedings in March.
The Adabor attack was also captured on CCTV, showing masked men and armed youth smashing cameras and striking the building with weapons. Police conducted overnight raids to arrest the six suspects.

headline_marked: Mumbai Police deny permit: [[Cockroach Janata Party calls for 'jail bharo' movement]]
headline: Mumbai Police deny permit: Cockroach Janata Party calls for 'jail bharo' movement
summary: The party is demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of bias toward the ruling BJP.
details: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has announced a 'jail bharo' (fill the jails) movement after Mumbai Police denied permission for a public protest at Shivaji Park on October 2.
The party is demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of ignoring other commissioners and acting in the interests of the ruling BJP.
Mumbai Police cited a 2013 Bombay High Court ruling that restricts Shivaji Park to sports activities, as well as concerns over noise pollution and traffic congestion in the residential area.
CJP leader Abhijit Dipke stated that the denial of permission is an attempt to suppress the voice of citizens and confirmed they will proceed with the movement on Gandhi Jayanti.
In a separate development, CJP leader Ashutosh Ranka and several local leaders were arrested in Assam during a 'fix the school' campaign.
Magsaysay award-winning educator and environmentalist Sonam Wangchuk has expressed his principled support for the CJP's movement for a transparent and neutral election process in India.
Wangchuk stated that while he may not be able to attend every protest personally, he believes the voice of the CJP will shake the entire country.
caption:
Denied a permit to protest, the Cockroach Janata Party is now calling for a 'jail bharo' movement in Mumbai.

The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has announced a 'jail bharo' (fill the jails) movement after Mumbai Police denied permission for a public protest at Shivaji Park on October 2.

The party is demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of ignoring other commissioners and acting in the interests of the ruling BJP.

Mumbai Police cited a 2013 Bombay High Court ruling that restricts Shivaji Park to sports activities, as well as concerns over noise pollution and traffic congestion in the residential area.

CJP leader Abhijit Dipke stated that the denial of permission is an attempt to suppress the voice of citizens and confirmed they will proceed with the movement on Gandhi Jayanti.

In a separate development, CJP leader Ashutosh Ranka and several local leaders were arrested in Assam during a 'fix the school' campaign.

Magsaysay award-winning educator and environmentalist Sonam Wangchuk has expressed his principled support for the CJP's movement for a transparent and neutral election process in India.

Wangchuk stated that while he may not be able to attend every protest personally, he believes the voice of the CJP will shake the entire country.
